title: 7.3 · Playtest party
name: Playtest party
summary: Teams hand in first, then three rotations: half host while half play two games and fill a 2 stars and a wish card for each, the halves swap, then makers tally their cards and send one fix message. Watching without helping is the hard skill; the one change has to come from what the testers said.
iCan: watch someone play my game without helping
collect 2 stars and a wish from different players
change one thing because of what testers said, and say why
materials: 2 stars and a wish cards printable (four faces and eight word tiles; four cards per tester)
the playtest protocol printable (one per team) and the role cards: Player, Watcher, Note-taker
the team folders with the captains' login cards
the class Games tab open on the teacher's device
doNow: What is the hardest part of watching someone play your game? Write one rule for yourself.
plan: Arrive, captains log in and hand in, Do Now
Explore: the protocol and the card on the projector
Playtest: two rotations of 5 minutes, then tally and one fix (8)

warmup.why: two retrieval items from build day (which had no warm-up of its own), one vocabulary item, one preview of today, one more from build day

do: Put the protocol on the projector: hand in first; three rotations; the roles Player, Watcher (the maker: silent, notes where the player hesitates) and Note-taker; the four rules: be specific, be kind, say what not who, never write a name.
Hold up a 2 stars and a wish card: four faces (fun, clear, fair, would play again) and one word tile from eight. Fill one for the frog quiz with the class.
say: Testers are not there to be nice to you. They are there to show you what your game does to a real player. Watch where they get stuck, and keep your hands in your lap.
The maker says thank you, and nothing else. Every answer gets written down, not argued with.
ask: Two testers say level 2 is confusing. What do you do next, and what do you not do?
explore.afterAsk: Change level 2 and test again; do not add more levels, and do not explain the level to the next tester. Write change one thing on the board.
explore.bigIdea: Different players notice different things; change one thing because of what they said.

play.handIn: captains hand in at the start of the period: a clean scan is visible to the class at once; a flagged build waits for a human and is played from the maker's screen
rotations: Rotation 1 (5 minutes): half the teams host; the other half play two games each and fill a 2 stars and a wish card for each (four faces and one word tile).
Rotation 2 (5 minutes): swap hosts and players.
Rotation 3 (8 minutes): makers tally their cards (count each face, count the word tiles), pick the one change the cards support, send one fix message, play it, and hand in again.
play.roles: Player · Watcher (the maker: silent, hands in the lap, notes where the player gets stuck) · Note-taker; the roles rotate, so everyone watches once
play.rules: be specific, be kind, say what not who, never write a name; the maker says thank you only
lookFors: a Watcher who helps: hands in the lap, notes only
a change nobody asked for: the one change has to come from the cards
a card with no word tile: the word is the wish
play.misconception: Kids think feedback means the tester did not like their game; the point is that different players notice different things, and the cards tell you which one thing to change.
earlyFinishers: play a third game and fill a card for it
count the class's most common word tile on the board

discuss: What did players do that you never expected?
Which card changed your mind about your game, and what did you change?
showMe: One team shows its tally on the projector: the four face counts, the word tiles, and the one fix message they sent.

exit.sentencePrompt: What did your testers say, and what one thing did you change because of it?

rubric.line: Other perspectives: feedback from different players
levels: Names one thing a tester said
Names what two or more testers said, with the tally
Says how different testers noticed different things, and which one they chose to act on and why

rubric.line: Test and fix: one change the feedback supports
levels: Names a change and the feedback it came from
Also tested the change with a player and says what happened

exit.paper: exit half-sheet (two per page) with the three items and the sentence frame

support: the card is faces and one tile: no writing needed
the Watcher holds a hands-in-lap card as a reminder
the fix message starter: Testers said ___. Please change ___.
stretch: a second round of ratings after the fix, recorded on the back of the card
count the whole class's word tiles and say which wish was most common

unpluggedTwin.title: Paper prototypes rotate the same way
materials: each team's paper prototype from build day
steps: Rotation 1: half the teams host their paper prototype (the maker turns the panels and stays silent); the others play two and fill a card for each.
Rotation 3: makers tally the cards, change one panel, and say which card made them change it.

subPlan: Do Now on paper, 3 minutes: the hardest part of watching someone play your game, and one rule for yourself.

Playtest with the paper prototypes: half the teams host (the maker turns the panels and does not talk), the others play two prototypes and fill a 2 stars and a wish card for each; swap after five minutes; then makers tally their cards and change one panel. No projector, no Builder and no login needed; the fix message waits for the teacher.
Paper exit ticket: the half-sheet with three questions and the sentence frame. Collect it with the cards.

a second round of ratings after the fix
10 minutes of the Unit 7 review on Brain Board

notes: Hand in at the start: a clean scan is visible to the class at once; a flagged build waits for a human and is played from the maker's screen today.
Watch the class Games tab during rotation 1: remove is one tap, and so is put back.
Testers' words reach the maker only through the paper cards or this lesson's question step; there is no in-game chat.
Captains sign in; the question step is the team's. Mark the Test with others line on it and use Also mark these teammates.
Collect the cards: two or more cards and one explained change is the Test with others line at 2; a second round of ratings after the change is a 3.
Roles rotate inside the team (Player, Watcher, Note-taker), which is why the roles id is practiced again today.

steps.title: Today
steps.body:
Do Now: What is the hardest part of watching someone play your game? Write one rule for yourself.

Big idea: Different players notice different things; change one thing because of what they said.

Today: hand in first, then three rotations. Host, play, then tally and fix one thing.

We will talk about:
- What did players do that you never expected?
- Which card changed your mind, and what did you change?

steps.title: Warm-up (live)
steps.body: Five quick questions. Your teacher shows them on the projector or starts them live.

steps.title: Playtest protocol
steps.body:
Hand in your game first.

Three rotations:
- Rotation 1: half the teams host, half play. Play two games. Fill one 2 stars and a wish card for each: four faces (fun, clear, fair, would play again) and one word tile.
- Rotation 2: swap.
- Rotation 3: makers tally the cards, pick one change, send one fix message, play it, hand in again.

Roles: Player · Watcher (the maker: silent, hands in your lap, note where the player gets stuck) · Note-taker.

Rules: be specific, be kind, say what not who, never write a name. The maker says thank you, and nothing else.

steps.title: Tally and the one change

levels: Attempted: one tester card, or cards with no change made
Meets: two or more tester cards tallied, one change made because of them and explained
Exceeds: a second round of ratings recorded after the change

steps.body:
Write your tally:
- How many cards did you get?
- Faces: how many smiles for fun, clear, fair, would play again?
- Which word tiles came up, and which came up most?
- The one change you made because of the cards, and the fix message you sent.
- What happened when you played it after the fix?

steps.title: Exit ticket
steps.body: Three quick questions about feedback and playtesting.

steps.title: In your own words
steps.body:
What did your testers say, and what one thing did you change because of it?
Frame: Testers said ___; I changed ___.
